V. INSPECTION AND ACCEPTANCE The Contractor shall provide to the U.S. Government the deliverables described in the Technical Specifications (Section I) of this Statement of Work. Further, the Contractor shall properly perform SENSITIVE BUT UNCLASSIFIED 9 SBU - CONTRACTING AND ACQUISITIONS all required testing, quality assurance, and validation on each Taskprior to submission for Government review. The final inspection and acceptance of ALL deliverables shall be performed by the U.S. Government upon completion and submission of the entire scope of work (Products 1 through 4). If INL Guatemala officials identify an incomplete, non- functional, or defective deliverable, they shall immediately refrain from accepting it and notify the Contractor in writing. Upon notification, the Contractor shall correct or replace the deficient deliverable at no additional cost to the Government. required for Task 3 (Production Deployment and User Acceptance Testing) and Task 4 (Knowledge Transfer). All coordination visits, deployment activities, and knowledge transfer sessions requiring physical presence shall take place at the GIO's institutional facilities in Guatemala City, Guatemala, as coordinated with the designated INL Guatemala point of contact. Remote work shall be permitted for all other tasks and activities where physical presence is not explicitly required, provided the Contractor maintains effective communication and coordination with INL Guatemala POC and the GIO throughout the period of performance. QUALITY ASSURANCE AND SURVEILLANCE PLAN (QASP) This plan provides an effective method to promote satisfactory contractor performance. The QASP provides a method for the Contracting Officer's Representative (COR) to monitor Contractor performance, advise the Contractor of unsatisfactory performance, and notify the Contracting Officer of continued unsatisfactory performance. The Contractor, not the Government, is responsible for management and quality control to meet the terms of the contract. To meet these ESR bunch injection schemes and requirements, an array of stripline-based kickers, individually fed by high voltage (HV) pulse signals of up to +/-30 kV, will be installed in the ESR. The required deflection angle is in the range 1- 1.5 mrad, for the individual stripline kicker we target a deflection angle of ~125 µrad @ 18 GeV, assuming +/-27 kV pulse supply voltage between the kicker electrodes. To keep the losses of the stored beam low, a ~15 σ distance between the stored beam and the injection septa in the ESR must be maintained, which translates into a minimum physical aperture of 30 mm diameter for the stripline kickers. Dokumenti hoiavad ajakohasena TEHIK arhitektid. The document defines the quality and non-functional requirements (NFRs) for new applications and their documentation. The document is maintained by the architects of the Health and Welfare Information Systems Centre (TEHIK). 1.2 Skoop / Scope Dokumenti tuleb vaadata kui arenduste kvaliteedi- ja mittefunktsionaalsete nõuete põhidokumenti. Nõudeid tuleb järgida ka olemasolevate rakenduste versiooniuuendustel nii palju kui versiooniuuenduse käigus võimalik. The document must be viewed as the principal document for quality and non-functional requirements for developments. The requirements must also be adhered to when upgrading existing applications to the extent possible during the upgrade process. 1.3 Terminid ja mõisted / Terms and definitions Kasutatakse standardseid IT-, rakenduste ja infosüsteemide valdkonna termineid. The purpose of this system is to detect anomalies in real-time through comparison of historical process conditions and real-time information; and also provide the means for users to access this data; to display high-quality graphics; plot and trend this data; and provide notification of equipment performance anomalies. The anomaly detection system must be designed to accommodate very large real-time and historical databases so that multiple anomaly detection models can be run simultaneously. The models must be scalable and efficient so that they can run at any interval up to once every 1 minute, as required by the end user. The results of all calculations must be stored on-line for years, in its original resolution preferably within Reclamation’s historian. The archive results must not in any way affect the calculated data from its original resolution and sampled state. With this high-resolution data available, users can view both the plant conditions and analytic results while providing a very clear and accurate picture of past operations. The system must also provide a method for managing and dispositioning alarms. Any dispositioned alarm should be easily accessible; users should be able to bring up a full analytic copy of all alarm information associated with a dispositioned alarm. The purpose of this system is to detect anomalies in real-time through comparison of historical process conditions and real-time information; and also provide the means for users to access this data; to display high-quality graphics; plot and trend this data; and provide notification of equipment performance anomalies. The anomaly detection system must be designed to accommodate very large real-time and historical databases so that multiple anomaly detection models can be run simultaneously. The models must be scalable and efficient so that they can run at any interval up to once every 1 minute, as required by the end user. The results of all calculations must be stored on-line for years, in its original resolution preferably within Reclamation’s historian. The archive results must not in any way affect the calculated data from its original resolution and sampled state. With this high-resolution data available, users can view both the plant conditions and analytic results while providing a very clear and accurate picture of past operations.
